questions.q: How does the force from prop imbalance depend on RPM?
questions.explain: The centrifugal force m·r·ω² grows with the square of angular velocity.

questions.q: How does a frame resonance differ from a motor peak in the spectrum?
options: It is always below 50 Hz on any frame and doesn't depend on size
It doesn't move when throttle changes
It is only on the 3rd harmonic
It is visible only on the accelerometer
questions.explain: A resonance is tied to the structure, while motor peaks follow RPM.

questions.q: Why doesn't the RPM filter remove frame resonance?
questions.explain: The RPM filter places notches on the harmonics of motor RPM. A fixed resonance is caught by the dynamic notch or eliminated by the structure.

questions.q: What happens when the accelerometer clips in ArduPilot?
options: The barometer switches to GPS altitude
The EKF loses its altitude estimate
questions.explain: A saturated accelerometer gives wrong data, which shows up in VIBE/Clip and leads to altitude drift.

questions.q: Why is a tight wire harness to the FC harmful with a soft mount?
options: It causes interference for the GPS and compass
It's a link that bypasses the dampers
questions.explain: Vibration travels through the tight wires straight into the board, and the dampers stop working.

questions.q: What is the motor's 1st-harmonic frequency at 12,000 rpm?
For a 5", the natural frequency of the board on its grommets should be:
questions.explain: 3–5 times below the motors, above the control bandwidth; too soft — mushiness and a low-frequency peak.

questions.q: Low-frequency shaking at 20–70 Hz most often comes from:
questions.explain: Prop wash is aerodynamics, low frequencies; imbalance is at the rotation frequency.
